fr.recommendations: Based on the observed site characteristics, maintaining clear and unobstructed internal drive aisles could improve responder movement and maneuvering throughout the property. While multiple access points exist along the street frontage and front entry area, limited access at the rear of the main building may affect responder positioning during operations, and identifying alternative approach routes in advance would support more efficient deployment. Dense vegetation within landscaped areas and open green spaces could reduce visibility for navigating personnel, and periodic management of those areas may enhance sightlines along travel corridors. Vehicle congestion within parking areas could restrict apparatus staging and movement, and coordinating with occupants to maintain clear pathways would assist emergency personnel in accessing all sides of the structure.

wildfire.recommendations: Reducing fuel continuity between scattered trees, tree clusters, and mixed vegetation cover across the property would improve defensible space and may reduce opportunities for fire spread toward structures. Vegetation growing adjacent to structures, including brush and shrubs in direct contact with or near building perimeters, should be managed to increase separation between fuels and structural components. Thinning and spacing vegetation within the immediate structure zone could reduce concentrated fuel loads and improve the overall defensible space envelope. The irrigated landscape present on the property represents a valuable low-fuel buffer that should be maintained and, where feasible, expanded to support fuel separation near improvements. Managing vegetation along the access route would support firefighter access and suppression operations by reducing fuel continuity and maintaining clear ingress and egress. Continued attention to the vegetated perimeter, including reducing shrub density and maintaining separation between individual plants, could improve long-term wildfire resilience and support property preparedness.
